content.text:
I have inspected every responsive location. Findings:

- **p0387–p0388** — "exclusive control" over the Cap Collateral Account is a securities-account control mechanic held *by the Issuer* (our party); not a sourcing covenant.
- **p0427** — "nonexclusive jurisdiction" is a forum term, not exclusivity.
- **p0080 / p0137 / p0150** — Section 3.1 Engagement and the Custodian/Marketing Agent appointments are bare appointments; none says Cellco is the sole or exclusive provider, and none bars the Issuer or Depositor from engaging others.
- **p0335** — the Successor Servicer machinery affirmatively lets the Issuer/Indenture Trustee engage another servicer, confirming no sole-source lock-in.
- No "requirements", "sole supplier", "shall not procure from any third party", or non-compete covenant binds our party anywhere.

The preferred position is satisfied on the document's own terms, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: Section 3.1 Engagement. The Issuer engages Cellco as the Servicer of the Receivables for the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee, and Cellco accepts this engagement.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on our side, so it meets the preferred position. Section 3.1 (p0080) and the parallel Custodian (p0137) and Marketing Agent (p0150) provisions are bare appointments of Cellco: none designates Cellco as sole or exclusive provider, and none bars the Issuer, Depositor or Indenture Trustee from engaging other providers. The Successor Servicer regime (p0335) affirmatively contemplates engaging a different servicer, confirming the absence of any lock-in. The word "exclusive" appears only in the Cap Collateral Account control mechanic (p0387-p0388), which is a control right held by the Issuer and therefore benefits our party, and in "nonexclusive jurisdiction" (p0427), a forum term. Searches for requirements-purchase, sole-source, "any third party" procurement bars and non-compete covenants returned nothing binding our party. No redline needed.
